question: Find the value of frac{{{{tan }²}60^circ + {{cot }²}30^circ }}{{{{tan }²}20^circ - {{sec }²}20^circ }} - frac{{sin 90^circ + cos 0^circ }}{{cos e{c²}20^circ - {{cot }²}20^circ }}.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Put standard trigonometric values and basic identities directly into the expression.

Use: tan² θ − sec² θ = −1 and cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1

Expression = [(√3)² + (√3)²] / (−1) − [1 + 1] / 1

= (3 + 3) / (−1) − (2) / 1

= −6 − 2 = −8

**∴ The correct answer is -8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(tan² 60° + cot² 30°) / (tan² 20° − sec² 20°) − (sin 90° + cos 0°) / (cosec² 20° − cot² 20°)

**Formula and Values Used:**

⇒ sec² θ − tan² θ = 1 ⇒ tan² θ − sec² θ = −1

⇒ cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1

⇒ tan 60° = √3, cot 30° = √3

⇒ sin 90° = 1, cos 0° = 1

**Calculations:**

⇒ First part numerator: tan² 60° + cot² 30° = (√3)² + (√3)² = 3 + 3 = 6

⇒ First part denominator: tan² 20° − sec² 20° = −1

⇒ Second part numerator: sin 90° + cos 0° = 1 + 1 = 2

⇒ Second part denominator: cosec² 20° − cot² 20° = 1

⇒ Expression Value = (6 / −1) − (2 / 1)

⇒ Value = −6 − 2 = −8

**∴ The correct answer is -8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 | 1 + tan² θ = sec² θ | 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ

Key Trigonometric Values

sin 90° = 1, cos 0° = 1, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3, cot 30° = √3.

Complementary Angles

sin(90° − θ) = cos θ | tan(90° − θ) = cot θ | sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ
